title: Mar son of Rav Yosef
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Rava’s student and always transmitted in his name: Shabbat 45b, Beitzah 27b, Gittin 72b, Bava Metzia 67a, Bava Batra 142b and Bekhorot 4a and 47a. In Shabbat 116a Rava was asked why he did not attend Bei Avidan and replied that the road was difficult for him. Mar son of Rav Yosef said: “I am one of them”—they are his acquaintances—“and I do not fear them.” Once he went, they sought to endanger him.

And he was the head (resh) in his town in the time of Rav Ashi, as in Chullin 48b: regarding a needle that was found in the liver, Mar, son of Rav Yosef, thought to declare it terefah. Rav Ashi said to him: "If one had found it in the flesh in such a manner, would the master have declared it terefah?"

notes.text: The first-person quotation ends before the narrative “once he went.” The latter is kept as narrative without inventing another speaker. The headship in his town is Hyman’s designation, without assigning a new formal office.

The consulted Shabbat 116a directly has Mar bar Yosef’s “I am one of them” and “I do not fear them,” followed by the narrator’s “once he went, they sought to endanger him.” Hyman’s acquaintance gloss, always-transmitted-in-Rava’s-name assertion and local headship remain attributed; no additional formal office or era is assigned.
